title: The machine as states and triggers
summary: Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25: instead of a set of scripts which do things, a machine is a set of event triggers which fire when a state has occurred. Linux is another producer of objects into the estate logging (logging is logging; the native providers are a pump to the log infrastructure and to objects). Logging going down is itself an event, handled by an operational handler. The arbitrator re-plans on events: a demand arrives or is withdrawn, a task ends or moves, pressure changes, the cluster answers.
authority: built and tested offline (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-25)
invariants: Observing a state and acting on it are separate permissions
Every action carries the event that caused it
A trigger fires only once its evidence is retained
Logging going down is an event for an operational handler (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25)
procedure: New behaviour on a machine is a registered trigger plus a handler, never a free-standing script
